positions.thesis: Massive 47% pullback from highs with +19% monthly recovery signals institutional washout completion. Oracle's cloud infrastructure is essential; the recovery momentum suggests market is repricing the opportunity.
evidence: It is about 47% below its high of the past year
positions.counterargument: The 47% drawdown may reflect genuine competitive threats from cloud-native vendors or margin compression that persists.

positions.thesis: Down only 2% YTD despite cloud/AI leadership suggests market has undervalued the stock; +12% monthly recovery and 23% off highs indicates bad news already reflected.
evidence: about 23% below its high of the past year
positions.counterargument: Weak YTD returns despite cloud narrative could mean valuation is already stretched at current levels relative to fundamentals.

positions.thesis: Only +7% YTD underperformance relative to mega-cap peers despite AI investments and chip development. 23% pullback and +5% monthly recovery suggest market discounting risks too heavily.
evidence: about 23% below its high of the past year
positions.counterargument: Regulatory scrutiny and difficulty monetizing metaverse investments could justify the underperformance and continue.

positions.thesis: Balanced risk/reward with +39% YTD and 20% off highs; market has repriced after correction without reaching euphoria. EV adoption thesis remains intact as evidenced by the recent recovery.
evidence: about 20% below its high of the past year
positions.counterargument: Intensifying competition in EV space and margin compression risks could weigh on returns despite historical momentum.

positions.thesis: 33% washout is overdone for quality software franchise with enterprise stickiness. Early recovery signals (+4% monthly) suggest capitulation complete; AI/enterprise adoption trends remain strong.
evidence: about 40% below its high of the past year
positions.counterargument: The 40% drawdown could reflect structural challenges to subscription model or competitive disruption from generative AI.

positions.thesis: Travel recovery thesis intact; 16% YTD decline and 27% off highs represent major opportunity as post-pandemic normalization persists. Market is pricing excessive caution.
evidence: about 27% below its high of the past year
positions.counterargument: Macro slowdown or recession could severely impact travel spending, especially if consumer savings are depleted.

positions.thesis: 24% YTD gain with 30% pullback and recent weakness (-2% monthly) suggests underperformance reset. Government contracts and AI positioning remain durable edges.
evidence: about 30% below its high of the past year
positions.counterargument: Reliance on government spending and expensive acquisition strategy make it vulnerable to political shifts or further valuation compression.

positions.thesis: Down 3% YTD but +10% monthly recovery shows momentum building. Core payments thesis intact; modest weight provides diversification to tech portfolio concentration.
positions.counterargument: Digital payments growth expectations are widely anticipated; competitive dynamics could pressure margins.

positions.thesis: Unsustainable 3542% YTD return with +71% monthly gain at all-time highs is textbook bubble. No reasonable fundamental supports 35x appreciation in twelve months; risk of violent mean reversion.
evidence: trading close to its highest point of the past year
positions.counterargument: If genuine structural market shift exists that benefits SNDK, gains could extend, though probability is minimal.

reasoning: Built concentrated position in high-conviction value names experiencing 20-47% pullbacks where bad news appears fully reflected in prices. Avoided egregious bubbles like SNDK (3542% YTD) while taking tactical short to exploit obvious mean reversion. Maintained 24% cash given 63-day lockup and binary outcome nature of the experiment; capital discipline is as important as stock selection.
